what: bench/compare.cpp on carsales (DS_CARS), arms MB_ENCODE, MB_FIELD and MB_READ, three trees: main = 9a6c192 (origin/main) extracted twice and built twice (main, main2: A/A), head = e50ce3d (branch schema-description, cbor::schema reads only cbor::describe_members). One binary per tree and arm. Also the compile time of test/schema.cpp of main and head, and cmp of the bytes that S::encode writes for the carsales value.
how: Trees from git archive. Build and run in podman, image mbedded-cbor-tw-compare, --network none, --cap-add SYS_NICE, --user 65534:65534. Build: g++-16 -std=c++26 -freflection -O2 -march=native -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64 -fPIE -pie -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -DDS_CARS -DOP_<arm>, 3 compilers at a time. Run: 7 rounds; in each round every binary once in shuffled order (shuf), --benchmark_min_time=1s, nice -n -10 when granted; a round with steal of 3 % or more is discarded and repeated (none was). Median of the 7 rounds; spread = max/min - 1. Compile time: g++-16 -std=c++26 -freflection -O2 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -c test/schema.cpp, 3 rounds, main and head in shuffled order per round; each tree compiles its own test/schema.cpp, and head has fewer test cases (the skip test is gone, one order test is new). The build lock was held from the first build to the last run. Scripts: bench/compare.cpp and a runner outside the tree; dump binary: compare.cpp with its main renamed and a main that writes S::encode(load()) to a file.
